title: Monitor: report Hyprland scale and persist named outputs

leads.summary: A failed copy of a staged named-rule update can empty monitors.lua but report success
leads.consequence: The redirection for cat opens/truncates the live file or symlink target before cat reads the stage file. A read/copy failure leaves a partially written or zero-byte config; the function unconditionally removes its stage file and returns 0, so set_scale proceeds as though persistence succeeded. On the next Hyprland reload the user's monitor rules and other contents are gone; the 2s poller does not recover those settings. Preserve the original until a checked, atomic replacement succeeds, and propagate failures.

leads.summary: The unconditional 1/120 normalization rejects otherwise exactly valid user-requested scales
leads.consequence: Hyprland first accepts a requested scale if the original pixel-size division is integral, before rounding to 1/120 units. For a valid 1088x680 mode, 1.0625 makes precisely 1024x640 logical pixels and Hyprland would retain 1.0625. The CLI instead sends 1.13333, and stores that changed scale; the panel's calculated value likewise differs from direct Hyprland behavior. Preserve an already-valid raw request before running the 1/120 nearest-neighbour search, with appropriate floating-point semantics.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-1.md) confirmed behaviour but same on base, only for unusual off-grid CLI values, earlier claim limited to on-grid; not published

leads.summary: Inserting a missing scale after a trailing inline comment writes the value into the comment, not the table
leads.consequence: For a valid multiline named rule whose last property ends `mode = "preferred", -- keep this`, the insertion scans raw bytes up to the final `}` and treats the final character of the comment as table content. It appends `, scale = 3` to the comment. awk exits successfully, so neither the catch-all nor fallback path runs; Hyprland's hl.monitor still has no scale field, so its default auto scale remains after reload despite the command reporting success. Insert before the comment in real Lua table syntax and assert the live field exists.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F4e shape, published under F5); corroboration

leads.summary: Open #13142 cannot be mechanically combined with this PR's scale/persistence changes
leads.consequence: #13142's promise is to preserve physical position on a live scale change (it sets the monitor's x/y), while this PR still evaluates a rule with `position = "auto"`. The two non-stacked PRs edit overlapping code and a merge of their actual head scripts against their own common base produces four conflict markers. Keeping this PR's eval during conflict resolution would drop #13142's positioning behavior and its new positioning test; the integrator needs to preserve its explicit x/y together with this PR's named-rule persistence.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified overlap with open #13142 from Sol's saved diff and gh pr view; Opus corrected wording against the public diff (D4)

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12263#issuecomment-5834033069) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12263#issuecomment-5835156860), checked at `3cab5084`. The branch was rebased; the three earlier commits are unchanged, and the new commit only touches `update_named_monitor_scale` and its test.

**Verified:** both fixes in the reply work. The new write-through has one new gap when the write fails (below).

| Earlier finding | Status at `3cab5084` |
|---|---|
| 2. Named-rule update replaces a symlinked `monitors.lua` | **Resolved** |
| 4. Missing `scale` after a trailing comma gives invalid Lua | **Resolved** |
| 1. Appended fallback rule overrides `desc:` rules and custom catch-alls | Still present, code unchanged |
| 3. Integer divisibility is not Hyprland's acceptance test | Still present, code unchanged |
| 5. Comments are edited as if they were live rules | Still present, comment handling unchanged |
| 6. Clamshell poller reverts multi-line internal rules | Still present, code unchanged |

### Resolved

**2. Symlinks:** absolute, relative and chained links to single-line and nwg-displays multi-line files all stay links, the target receives the new scale, other rules are unchanged, and no temp files are left behind. The new test fails against the previous script and passes at this head, so it guards the regression. It covers only the single-line shape.

**4. Trailing comma:** a multi-line or single-line rule ending in `,` now gets `mode = "preferred", scale = 1.6` and parses with `luac`. A rule whose last field ends in `;` (also valid Lua) still gets `;, scale = 1.6`, which does not parse; this was the same before the commit and is a rare shape. Adding `;` to the same check covers it.

### Still present

Findings 1, 3, 5 and 6 reproduce at this head as originally described, including every number in the finding 3 table; the code behind them is identical to the earlier head (for finding 5, the new commit changed only the separator, not the comment handling). For finding 5, one more shape: when the last field line of a rule without `scale` ends in a comment (`mode = "preferred", -- panel mode`), the inserted `scale = X` lands inside the comment, the script reports success, and nothing is persisted. Stripping comments before matching, as suggested earlier, and before choosing the insertion point covers this too.

### New: a failed write-through still reports success

`update_named_monitor_scale` now finishes with:

```bash
cat "$tmp" >"$file"
rm -f "$tmp"
return 0
```

The status of `cat` is ignored, the complete temp copy is always deleted, and the function returns success.

| Case (stubbed `hyprctl`, request 1.6) | This head | Previous head / base |
|---|---|---|
| `monitors.lua` read-only (0444) in a writable directory | `Permission denied` on stderr, file unchanged, other fallbacks skipped, exit 0 | previous head: persisted (`mv` replaced the file); base: persisted through Omarchy's scale variable when present |
| Write fails partway (injected: 40 bytes written, then ENOSPC) | `monitors.lua` truncated and no longer valid Lua, temp copy deleted, exit 0 | previous head's `mv` was atomic |
| Link into a non-writable directory, writable target, file with only named rules | temp file cannot be created, treated as "no named rule"; a second same-name rule with `mode = "preferred", position = "auto"` is appended and overrides the user's mode and position; exit 4 | previous head replaced the link; base left the file untouched |

**Impact:** uncommon triggers (full disk, I/O error, read-only files or directories), but the partial-write case leaves a `monitors.lua` that Hyprland cannot load while reporting success.

**Suggested change:** check the write, keep the staged copy on failure and return a code the caller treats as fatal, for example:

```bash
if ! cat "$tmp" >"$file"; then
  echo "Could not write $file; update kept in $tmp" >&2
  return 2
fi
rm -f "$tmp"
```

Then have `set_scale` stop when it returns 2. Today its `if … elif` chain treats any failure as "no named rule" and falls through to the variable and append paths. Also distinguish a failure to create the temp file from "no named rule" for the same reason.

**Related PR:** open #13142 changes the live `hyprctl eval` line next to this PR's changes (keeping the current position instead of `auto`) and rewrites the same persistence block with its own named-rule update, so whichever lands second will need to reconcile both.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the new commit and rebase against Hyprland v0.56.2 (scale search unchanged on current main) and nwg-displays v0.4.4. The real scaling and clamshell scripts ran in isolated sandboxes with a stubbed `hyprctl` in 20 `monitors.lua` scenarios at this head, the previous head and base; results were checked with `luac` and Lua and Python transcriptions of Hyprland's rule lookup and scale search. The disk-full case used fault injection. The changed repository tests pass at this head, with the JavaScript test under Node. No live compositor was used.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
